newsitem.title: CANADA: Gulf signs land deal with Alberta Indians.
newsitem.headline: Gulf signs land deal with Alberta Indians.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd said on Monday it signed a land access agreement with an Alberta native group, the company's second deal with North American Indians in the past four months.
Gulf Canada said it signed an exclusive lease with the Four Nations of Hobbema for the right to explore for oil and gas on their 4,800-acre reserve at Pigeon Lake, Alberta.

The lease, which calls for a 3D seismic program, up to two well re-entries and a commitment to drill up to two new wells, was approved by the Samson Cree Nation, the Ermineskin Nation, the Louis Bull Nation and the Montana Nation, the company said.
In December, Gulf Canada signed an agreement with the Sioux and Assiniboine tribes of Fort Peck, Montana, giving it access to 110,000 acres of exploration lands in that state.
Besides paying an undisclosed bonus, Gulf Canada said it would agreed to establish a C$50,000 college scholarship for members of the four Indian nations.
It said operations would be carried out under a joint agreement between Gulf Canada, with a 75 percent interest, and Native Power Canada Corp, with 25 percent.
